decisions.summary: The push's in-progress refusal no longer refuses a feature whose spec status line begins with a closing word (Done / Superseded by / Withdrawn), though boxes stay unticked.
decisions.why: It narrows a standing guard, but the accepted spec requires it: FR-004 closes features by editing the status line and D3 (accepted) leaves their tasks unticked, so a refusal that still counts those open boxes would treat every FR-004 closure as in-progress work on every push that touches it - the literal old rule defeats the request's purpose (one true, mechanical state). The plan refuses the same word-exemption for the review gate, where nothing in the request implies it; here FR-002/FR-004 do.

decisions.summary: As implemented by 'refuse exactly what make speckit-todo calls planned or in progress', the refusal also swaps its box reader from any open box ('^\s*- \[ \]') to column-0 tasks only, and does not refuse state 'filed' even when a tasks.md exists.
decisions.why: Nothing in request.md or spec.md implies this part, and it inverts the spec's own edge case ('a parsing miss shows up as open work, not as finished work'): for the push guard a parsing miss now LANDS. Measured 2026-10-08 on fixtures run through speckit-todo.py --state: a tasks.md of indented '  - [ ] T01 / T02' reads 'filed' (old rule: refused; new: lands with every task open); a tasks.md with '- [x] T01' and an indented open '  - [ ] research pass' reads 'closed' (old: refused; new: lands). Zero current specs/ are in either shape (measured the same day), so the fix costs nothing today. Also fail-open: if the python call errors or prints nothing, the case matches no arm and the feature is not refused. Fix: keep the old open-box test and exempt only a closing status line - refuse when tasks.md has any '^\s*- \[ \]' line AND speckit-todo's state is not closed-by-status (or: refuse unless state is closed with a closing-word reason, and refuse on empty/failed output); add the two fixture cases above to test-sync-with-main.sh.

decisions.summary: review-gate.sh exempts from the fidelity-verdict check a spec whose status opens 'Filed' and whose directory has no tasks.md; gaining tasks.md ends the exemption.
decisions.why: Implied by the request: the GM asked that future-work entries 'become an unimplemented spec kit feature', and FR-006/FR-008 make filing (verbatim text, status Filed, no plan or tasks) the routine way to defer work. A filed spec implements nothing, and constitution XVI's review is before implementation; without the exemption every deferral needs an escape. The exemption is narrow: it keys on both the Filed status AND no tasks.md, ends when tasks appear (tested both ways), and opens nothing the gate held, since code pushed without touching the spec directory was never under this check.

decisions.summary: The one push of the 22 status-line rewrites carries REVIEW_GATE_OK with a reason, rather than a gate exemption for Done.
decisions.why: A single recorded escape for FR-004's status edits to specs that mostly predate the fidelity review; no guard is changed, and declining a Done exemption keeps the gate from being skipped by writing a word.
